title: Canonical truncation triangle in the derived category
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category, $D(\mathcal C)$ its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with cohomology functors $H^n$, and let $K\in D(\mathcal C)$ and $b\in\mathbf Z$. There is a distinguished triangle
$$
K'\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow K''\longrightarrow K'[1]
$$
with $H^n(K')=0$ for all $n>b-1$ and $H^n(K'')=0$ for all $n<b$ (namely $K'=	au_{\leq b-1}K$, $K''=	au_{\geq b}K$ for the canonical t-structure).

source.place: Derived Categories, Remark Tag 08J5 (label remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle: the canonical triangle $\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to\tau_{\geq a+1}K\to$, from the short exact sequence $0\to\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to K/\tau_{\leq a}K\to0$), with $a=b-1$
